section_1.title: The Hook: The Broken Pencil Illusion
section_1.content: Introduce the phenomenon by showing a pencil in a half-full glass of water. Explain that light changes direction when moving between media, creating a visual 'break'.
section_1.example: An animation of a pencil submerged in water; the submerged portion appears shifted upward due to light rays bending at the air-water interface.

section_2.title: Prerequisite: The Wave Nature of Light
section_2.content: Briefly define light as a wave with speed (v), frequency (f), and wavelength (λ). Establish that light travels fastest in a vacuum and slows down in denser materials (optical density).
section_2.example: Visual metaphor: A marching band moving from smooth pavement (fast) to thick mud (slow) at an angle, causing the rows to rotate/turn.

section_3.title: The Mechanism: Snell’s Law
section_3.content: Define the Refractive Index (n = c/v). Present Snell's Law: n1 * sin(θ1) = n2 * sin(θ2). Use a diagram showing the 'Normal' line, the Angle of Incidence (θ1), and the Angle of Refraction (θ2).
section_3.example: An interactive animation overlay: Adjusting the laser angle (θ1) shows the refracted beam (θ2) responding in real-time according to the calculated index of refraction.

section_4.title: Real-World Application: The Archer Fish
section_4.content: Apply the concept to nature. Explain how an Archer Fish compensates for refraction when spitting water at insects above the surface by aiming 'below' where the prey appears to be.
section_4.example: A side-profile animation showing the fish 'calculating' the refraction shift to successfully hit a beetle perched on an overhanging branch.

section_5.title: Synthesis & Summary
section_5.content: Summarize that refraction occurs due to a change in speed when entering a new medium. Reiterate that light bends toward the normal when slowing down, and away when speeding up.
section_5.example: A quick-fire graphical summary: Light entering glass (fast to slow, bends toward normal) vs. light exiting glass (slow to fast, bends away from normal).

        self.play(Write(snells_law))

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 2 ===
        self.lecture[0].set_color(WHITE)
        self.lecture[1].set_color("#FFFF00")
        
        # Setup Diagram elements
        boundary = Line(self.grid["D1"], self.grid["D6"], color=WHITE)
        normal = DashedLine(self.grid["B4"], self.grid["F4"], color=GRAY)
        
        # Incident Ray

from manim import *
import numpy as np

class TeachingScene(Scene):
    def setup_layout(self, title_text, lecture_lines):
        # BASE
        self.camera.background_color = "#000000"
        self.title = Text(title_text, font_size=28, color=WHITE).to_edge(UP)
        self.add(self.title)

        # Left-side lecture content (bullets with "-")
        lecture_texts = [Text(line, font_size=22, color=WHITE) for line in lecture_lines]
        self.lecture = VGroup(*lecture_texts).arrange(DOWN, aligned_edge=LEFT).scale(0.8)
        self.lecture.to_edge(LEFT, buff=0.2)
        self.add(self.lecture)

        # Define fine-grained animation grid (4x4 grid on right side)
        self.grid = {}
        rows = ["A", "B", "C", "D", "E", "F"]  # Top to bottom
        cols = ["1", "2", "3", "4", "5", "6"]  # Left to right

        for i, row in enumerate(rows):
            for j, col in enumerate(cols):
                x = 0.5 + j * 1
                y = 2.2 - i * 1
                self.grid[f"{row}{col}"] = np.array([x, y, 0])

    def place_at_grid(self, mobject, grid_pos, scale_factor=1.0):
        mobject.scale(scale_factor)
        mobject.move_to(self.grid[grid_pos])
        return mobject

    def place_in_area(self, mobject, top_left, bottom_right, scale_factor=1.0):
        tl_pos = self.grid[top_left]
        br_pos = self.grid[bottom_right]
        
        # Calculate center of the area
        center_x = (tl_pos[0] + br_pos[0]) / 2
        center_y = (tl_pos[1] + br_pos[1]) / 2
        center = np.array([center_x, center_y, 0])
        
        mobject.scale(scale_factor)
        mobject.move_to(center)
        return mobject

class Section2Scene(TeachingScene):
    def construct(self):
        self.setup_layout("Prerequisite: The Wave Nature of Light", [
            "Light travels as a wave at speed v.",
            "Materials affect speed based on density.",
            "Think of a band entering thick mud."
        ])

            "Light bends when moving between media.",

        ])
        
        # Asset Loading (Placeholders)
        prism = SVGMobject("/scratch/pawsey1357/jthen/Code2Video/assets/icon/prism.svg")
        laser = SVGMobject("/scratch/pawsey1357/jthen/Code2Video/assets/icon/laser.svg")
